title: Chicken à la Kiev
description: A classic Continental dish featuring tender chicken breast stuffed with herb butter, coated in crisp breadcrumbs, and cooked until golden with a rich molten center.

ingredients.title: For the Herb Butter Filling (Beurre Maître d’Hôtel)
For the Chicken
items: Breadcrumbs (fine panko or fresh white) – 1 cup
Clarified butter – 1 tbsp (optional, for finishing in oven)

instruction.title: Step 1 – Prepare the Compound Butter
steps: In a bowl, combine softened butter, parsley, garlic, lemon juice, salt, and pepper.
Shape into a log using cling film, roll tightly, and freeze until firm (about 30 minutes).

instruction.title: Step 2 – Prepare the Chicken
steps: Butterfly each chicken breast, creating a deep pocket or flatten gently with a mallet between cling films — about 1 cm thick.
Season lightly with salt and white pepper.
Slice the chilled butter into thick pieces and place one in the center of each breast.
Fold the sides inward and roll tightly like a parcel, sealing all edges to prevent leakage.
Wrap in cling film and freeze for 20–25 minutes to firm up.

instruction.title: Step 3 – Coat and Crumb
steps: Dredge each chicken roll in flour (shake off excess).
Dip in beaten egg, then coat evenly with breadcrumbs.
For an extra-crisp shell, repeat the egg and breadcrumb coating once more.
Chill for 10 minutes to set the crust.

instruction.title: Step 4 – Fry and Finish
steps: Heat oil to 170°C (340°F) in a deep fryer or heavy pan.
Fry each chicken roll until golden brown, about 5–6 minutes, turning occasionally.
Transfer to a baking tray and finish in a preheated oven (180°C / 350°F) for 7–10 minutes, or until the internal temperature reaches 74°C (165°F).

servingSuggestions.title: Serving Suggestions
items: Serve with pommes purée (silky mashed potatoes) or truffled potato fondant.
Pair with French beans almondine or buttered asparagus tips.
Finish with a light drizzle of herb butter reduction or lemon beurre blanc.
Garnish with microgreens and a lemon wedge for brightness.

chefTips: Seal well: Any gaps in the chicken will cause the butter to leak during cooking.
Freeze before frying: This helps keep the butter intact and ensures a perfect molten center.
Double-crumbing ensures a crisp, restaurant-style crust.
Use clarified butter for finishing—it adds richness and a golden sheen.
